title: Review of c10's active-PFC births finding: replicated on fresh seeds 7 and 8, births are templated next to existing peaks, never a split
summary: Re-ran the claimed world (kappa=0) with labkit on seed 7 (rerun/seed7, 120 frames to t=600) and ran the author's births.py census, unchanged, on seeds 7 and 8 for both the conserved world and kappa=0.002, psi0=-0.70 (births_c16.txt). Every birth on both seeds and both arms lies within 12 px of a peak that existed 2 t earlier (median 8.55-9.0 px against the 9.2 px lattice spacing), with 0-1 losses per run; peaks grow 15->28 and 12->18 (conserved) and 15->50 and 12->44 (kappa 0.002). The labkit lineage on seed 7 shows 31 splits with 32 merges and only 1 persistent split (max generation 1), and the sheet shows new peaks appearing on the flank of existing pairs and rafts, never one peak becoming two. The finding replicates: the class gives I and M plus templated crystal growth, not reproduction.

observations.I: rerun/seed7/sheet.png: 15 isolated round peaks by t=25 persist, joined by later ones, to t=600
observations.M: rerun/seed7/sheet.png: single peaks and rafts change position between frames t=25-600
observations.finding: births_c16.txt: 13/37/6/32 births, 100% within 12 px of an earlier peak, median 8.6/8.9/9.0/8.55 px; rerun/seed7/lineage.png: 1 persistent split, max gen 1

controls_run.finding: births_c16.txt: kappa=0 and kappa=0.002/psi0=-0.70 arms on seeds 7 and 8 (author's births.py, unchanged)

verdicts.limitation: Same census code and grid as the author; I did not vary dt or resolution, and 'never a split' rests on the census rule (new peak with no peak within 3 px) plus the labkit lineage and visual inspection of seed 7, not on a per-event birth strip of my own.
